   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">AEye, Inc. and its wholly owned subsidiaries&#160;(the &#8220;Company&#8221; or &#8220;AEye&#8221;)&#160;is a provider of physical AI sensing solutions built on high-performance, active lidar systems for vehicle autonomy, advanced driver-assistance systems, or ADAS,&#160;robotic vision applications and a range of Non-Automotive applications.&#160;Our approach to supporting the developing physical AI infrastructure combines software&#8209;defined sensing with adaptive perception capabilities that enable machines to interpret and respond to complex physical environments in real time. Our proprietary Intelligent Sensing Platform incorporates a nearly solid state, software&#8209;definable active lidar sensor; an adaptive SmartScan architecture that dynamically adjusts scan patterns for different scenes and targets; and a signal processing pipeline designed to deliver precise measurements and imaging for safety critical use cases. This platform is designed to support a broad set of markets beyond passenger vehicles, including rail, aerospace and defense, smart infrastructure, and security, where long&#8209;range performance, environmental robustness, and software&#8209;based configurability are key requirements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">AEye, formerly known as CF Finance Acquisition Corp. III, (&#8220;CF III&#8221;), was originally incorporated in Delaware on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 15, 2016 </em>under the name CF SPAC Re Inc. On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 17, 2021, </em>AEye Technologies, Inc., then known as AEye, Inc., entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with CF III. Based on CF III&#8217;s business activities, it was a &#8220;shell company&#8221; as defined under the Securities Exchange Act of <em style="font: inherit;">1934,</em> as amended. On <em style="font: inherit;"> August 16, 2021, </em>the business combination contemplated by the Agreement and Plan of Merger was closed and CF III changed its name to AEye, Inc.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company&#8217;s common stock and public warrants are listed on the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (&#8220;Nasdaq&#8221;) under the symbols &#8220;LIDR&#8221; and &#8220;LIDRW&#8221;, respectively. Unless otherwise specified, &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;us,&#8221; &#8220;our,&#8221; &#8220;AEye,&#8221; and the &#8220;Company&#8221; refers to AEye, Inc.&#160;and its wholly owned subsidiaries.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The accompanying condensed consolidated financial statements are unaudited and have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) for interim financial statements and pursuant to the rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission. Accordingly, they do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include all of the information and footnotes required by GAAP for complete financial statements. In the opinion of management, all adjustments considered necessary for fair presentation have been included. The accompanying interim unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements should be read in conjunction with the audited consolidated financial statements and related notes thereto included in the Company's Annual Report on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>

Actual results could differ from those estimates.&#160;Significant items subject to such estimates and assumptions include write-downs of inventory to the lower of cost or net realizable value, investments, embedded derivative and warrant liabilities, stock-based compensation,&#160;and convertible notes.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company has funded its operations primarily through the issuances of common stock. Since its inception, the Company has incurred net losses and negative cash flows from operations and expects to incur additional operating losses and negative operating cash flows as management continues to focus on achieving commercialization of its lidar solutions and execute on its strategic initiatives.&#160; As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the Company&#8217;s existing sources of liquidity included cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145963447" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CashCashEquivalentsAndShortTermInvestments" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">77,238</ix:nonFraction>.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskCreditRisk" id="c145964890" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Concentration of Credit Risk</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Financial instruments which potentially subject the Company to concentration of credit risk consist primarily of cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, and accounts receivable, net. The Company places its cash and cash equivalents with major financial institutions, which management assesses to be of high credit quality, to limit the exposure of each investment. The Company&#8217;s marketable securities have investment grade ratings when purchased&#160;which mitigates risk.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company&#8217;s accounts receivable, net are derived from customers located in North America,&#160;Europe, the Middle East,&#160;Africa (EMEA), and&#160;the Asia-Pacific (APAC)&#160;region. The Company mitigates its credit risks by performing ongoing credit evaluations of its customers&#8217; financial conditions. The Company generally does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> require collateral.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c145964891" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> <i>Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses</i>, which requires annual and interim disclosure of disaggregated disclosures of certain costs and expenses on the income statement. The standard is effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim periods within fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027, </em>with early adoption permitted. Amendments are applied on a prospective basis with retrospective application permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of this guidance.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;"></p>
  </ix:nonNumeric>
  <div>
    &#160;
  </div>
  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="c3203351" escape="true">
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">2.</em></b><b> </b></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENTS</b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The fair value of the Company&#8217;s financial assets and liabilities is determined in accordance with the fair value hierarchy established in FASB ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">820,</em> <i>Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures</i> (&#8220;ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820&#8221;</em>). ASC&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">820</em> defines fair value as the exchange price that would be received for an asset or paid to transfer a liability (an exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date. The fair value hierarchy of ASC&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">820</em> requires an entity to maximize the use of observable inputs when measuring fair value and classifies those inputs into <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> levels:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Level</i></b>&#160;<b><i><em style="font: inherit;">1</em></i></b>&#8212;Observable inputs, such as quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Level</i></b>&#160;<b><i><em style="font: inherit;">2</em></i></b>&#8212;Observable inputs, other than Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> inputs, which are observable either directly or indirectly or can be corroborated by observable market data using quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><i>Level</i></b>&#160;<b><i><em style="font: inherit;">3</em></i></b>&#8212;Unobservable inputs in which there is little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market data, which require the reporting entity to develop its own assumptions.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company's financial instruments that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> remeasured at fair value include accounts receivable, prepaid and other current assets, accounts payable, accrued expenses, other current and noncurrent liabilities, and the noncurrent convertible&#160;note. The carrying values of these financial instruments approximate their fair values.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Marketable Securities</i>: The Company holds financial assets consisting of fixed-income U.S. government securities, corporate bonds,&#160;commercial paper, agency bonds, and asset-backed securities. The securities are valued using prices from independent pricing services based on quoted prices of identical instruments in less active or inactive markets.&#160; Additionally, quoted prices of similar instruments in active market or industry models using data inputs such as interest rates and prices that can be directly observed or corroborated in active markets are used to value marketable securities.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt -9pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Derivative</i> <i>Warrant Liabilities:</i> On <em style="font: inherit;"> September 15, 2022</em>, the Company entered into a convertible note agreement with a face value of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145963485" contextRef="i_2022-09-15_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2022NoteMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-ConvertibleDebtMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">10,500</ix:nonFraction>&#160;(the <em style="font: inherit;">"2022</em> Note"). The Company issued&#160;warrants as part of the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Note. The warrants were recorded on the condensed consolidated balance sheets at fair value. The fair value is based on unobservable inputs, which represent Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> measurements within the fair value hierarchy. The fair value estimate of the warrants was based on a Monte-Carlo simulation model. Inherent in a Monte-Carlo simulation model are assumptions related to price, volatility, risk-free interest rate, term to expiration, and dividend yield. Changes in fair value were recognized in other income (expense) for each reporting period. Derivative Warrant Liability was included within other noncurrent liabilities on the condensed consolidated balance sheets. These warrants were cancelled on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 28, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> January&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> the Company entered into a convertible note agreement with a face value of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145963490" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-ConvertibleDebtMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">3,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;(the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">"2025</em>&#160;Note"). The Company issued a warrant&#160;to purchase up to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145963492" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-The2025NoteWarrantsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">805,263</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock. The warrant was recorded on the accompanying consolidated balance sheet at fair value.&#160;The fair value was based on unobservable inputs, which represent Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> measurements within the fair value hierarchy. The fair value estimate of the warrants was based on a Black-Scholes&#160;model. Inherent in a Black-Scholes model are assumptions related to price, volatility, risk-free interest rate, term to expiration, and dividend yield.&#160;Changes in fair value were recognized in other income (expense) for each reporting period. Derivative Warrant Liability was included within other noncurrent liabilities on the condensed consolidated balance sheets. These warrants were exercised in full on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 28, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> August&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> in connection with the lease settlement (see Note <em style="font: inherit;">5</em> for details of the settlement), the Company issued&#160;warrants, which are&#160;recorded on the accompanying condensed consolidated balance sheets at fair value. The fair value is based on unobservable inputs, which represent Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> measurements within the fair value hierarchy. The fair value estimate of the warrants was based on a Black-Scholes&#160;model. Inherent in a Black-Scholes model are assumptions related to price, volatility, risk-free interest rate, term to expiration, and dividend yield.&#160;Changes in fair value are recognized in other income (expense) for each reporting period. Derivative Warrant Liability is included within other noncurrent liabilities on the condensed consolidated balance sheets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><i>Private Placement Warrant Liability</i>: The Private Placement Warrants are recorded on the condensed consolidated balance sheets at fair value. The fair value is based on observable Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> inputs, specifically, the observable input of the Company's public warrants, as terms of both warrants are substantially similar. Any changes in the fair value of the liability are reflected in other income (expense), net, on the condensed consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive loss. Private Placement Warrant liability is included within other noncurrent liabilities on the condensed consolidated balance sheets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 10, 2024</em>, the Company entered into a Securities Purchase Agreement with an investor for the sale and issuance of <ix:nonFraction id="c145963728" contextRef="d_2024-05-10_2024-05-10_CounterpartyNameAxis-AnInvestorMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SecurityPurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">330,823</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of common stock and a <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-05-10_2024-05-10_CounterpartyNameAxis-AnInvestorMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-ConvertibleNote2024Member" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentTerm" id="c145963729" format="ixt-sec:duryear">5</ix:nonNumeric>-year promissory note with a principal balance of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145963730" contextRef="i_2024-05-10_CounterpartyNameAxis-AnInvestorMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-ConvertibleNote2024Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">146</ix:nonFraction> (<em style="font: inherit;"> &#8220;May 2024 </em>Note&#8221;) for total gross cash proceeds of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963731" contextRef="d_2024-05-10_2024-05-10_CounterpartyNameAxis-AnInvestorMember" unitRef="USD" name="lidr:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfCommonStockAndDebt" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1,000</ix:nonFraction>. The <em style="font: inherit;"> May 2024 </em>Note bears interest at an annual rate equal to the Secured Overnight Financing Rate plus <ix:nonFraction id="c145963732" contextRef="d_2024-05-10_2024-05-10_CounterpartyNameAxis-AnInvestorMember_DebtInstrumentAxis-ConvertibleNote2024Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">1.0</ix:nonFraction>%, which is compounded quarterly in arrears, and has a maturity date of <em style="font: inherit;"> June 4, 2029</em>.    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Convertible Note</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> January&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> the Company entered into a Securities Purchase Agreement with a certain institutional investor and issued (i) a senior&#160;unsecured convertible promissory note (the <em style="font: inherit;">"2025</em> Note")&#160;for an aggregate principal amount of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145963737" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">3,240</ix:nonFraction> for an aggregate purchase&#160;price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963738" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromConvertibleDebt" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">3,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and (ii) a&#160;warrant&#160;to purchase up to <ix:nonFraction id="c145963739" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-The2025NoteWarrantsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ClassOfWarrantOrRightNumberOfSecuritiesCalledByWarrantsOrRights" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">805,263</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock. The <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Note, subject to an original issue discount of <ix:nonFraction id="c145963741" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="Pure" name="lidr:DebtInstrumentOriginalIssueDiscountRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">7.4</ix:nonFraction>%, had&#160;a term of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145963742">eighteen</span> months and accrued&#160;interest at the rate of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145963743" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">7</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;per annum.&#160;The interest <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be settled in cash or shares at the option of the Company and is payable together with monthly redemptions of the outstanding principal amount of the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Note. The <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Note was convertible into Common Stock, at a per share conversion price equal to $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963746" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentConvertibleConversionPrice1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2.22</ix:nonFraction>, subject to adjustments noted in the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Note.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">Monthly redemptions began in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> April 2025&#160;</em>and were&#160;due on the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">first</em>&#160;of each subsequent month (each a "Monthly Redemption Date" or an "Installment Date").&#160;The Company was required to redeem the Monthly Redemption Amount until the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note was fully redeemed, paid&#160;in cash or, so long as certain equity conditions are met, shares of our common stock. The investor was permitted to accelerate up to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;Monthly&#160;Installment Amount,&#160;between Installments.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company elected to apply the fair value option to the measurement of the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note. As a result of adopting the fair value option,&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;embedded derivatives are bifurcated from the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note. The Company classified&#160;the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note as a liability at fair value and remeasured the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note to fair value at each reporting period. The total proceeds received from the investor of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963757" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromConvertibleDebt" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">3,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;was allocated between the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note and the related warrants issued using the relative fair value method at issuance date. This resulted in an initial fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963759" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ConvertibleDebtFairValueDisclosures" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">3,266</ix:nonFraction>&#160;being allocated to the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963761" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_ClassOfWarrantOrRightAxis-The2025NoteWarrantsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:WarrantsAndRightsOutstanding" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,046</ix:nonFraction>&#160;allocated to the associated warrants. The Company recorded&#160;a non-cash issuance cost&#160;of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963762" contextRef="i_2025-01-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredFinanceCostsNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">1,312</ix:nonFraction>,&#160;representing the difference between the fair value and proceeds received, within Interest expense and other on the condensed consolidated statement of operations. The fair value measurement included&#160;the assumption of accrued interest and expense and thus a separate amount was&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;reflected on the condensed consolidated statement of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">During&#160;the year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>,&#160;the Company made cash payments of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963764" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RepaymentsOfDebt" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">989</ix:nonFraction>. Additionally,&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145963765" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_DebtConversionByUniqueDescriptionAxis-ConversionOfThe2025NoteIntoCommonStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtConversionOriginalDebtAmount1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,591</ix:nonFraction> in aggregate principal and interest were converted into&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145963766" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_DebtConversionByUniqueDescriptionAxis-ConversionOfThe2025NoteIntoCommonStockMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:DebtConversionConvertedInstrumentSharesIssued1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,405,573</ix:nonFraction> shares of&#160;common stock.&#160; As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025,&#160;</em>the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Note was fully repaid and all associated warrants were fully exercised.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><b>New Circle Principal Investments LLC (</b>&#8220;<b>New Circle</b>&#8221;<b>) Common Stock Purchase Agreement (the </b>&#8220;<b>CSPA</b>&#8221;<b>)</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 25, 2024</em>, the Company entered into a&#160;CSPA and a Registration Rights Agreement with New Circle. Under the terms and subject to the conditions of the CSPA, the Company had&#160;the right, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the obligation, to sell to New Circle, and New Circle was obligated to purchase up to the lesser of (i) $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963794" contextRef="i_2024-07-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="lidr:EquityOfferingMaximumAmount" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">50,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;of the Company&#8217;s common stock, or&#160;(ii) the Exchange Cap equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c145963795" contextRef="i_2024-07-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="lidr:EquityOfferingExchangeCapShares" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,721,755</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of the Company's common stock, unless the Company&#8217;s stockholders approve the issuance of shares in excess of the Exchange Cap, or the average price of all applicable sales of common stock to New Circle equals or exceeds <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145963796">$1.41</span>&#160;per share. The Company had&#160;sole discretion to initiate such sales of common stock over a&#160;period of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-07-25_2024-07-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" name="lidr:EquityOfferingPeriod" id="c145963797" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">36</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;months.&#160;In all instances, the Company could <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> sell shares of its common stock to New Circle under the CSPA if doing so would result in New Circle beneficially owning more than <ix:nonFraction id="c145963799" contextRef="i_2024-07-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="lidr:EquityOfferingMaximumBeneficialOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">4.99</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;of the Company's common stock.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The purchase price per share to be purchased by New Circle would equal either (i) the lowest volume-weighted average price for common stock either over a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-day trading period or <ix:nonFraction id="c145963802" contextRef="i_2024-07-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="lidr:EquityOfferingPurchasePricePercentageOfVolumeWeightedAveragePriceForOneDayOrIntradayTradingPeriod" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">15</ix:nonFraction> minutes after the number of intraday shares traded exceeds <em style="font: inherit;">500%</em> of the shares included in the&#160;purchase notice or <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> hour after the receipt of the purchase notice, or (ii) the volume-weighted average price for common stock for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> consecutive trading days commencing on the purchase notice date multiplied by <ix:nonFraction id="c145963806" contextRef="i_2024-07-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Pure" name="lidr:EquityOfferingPurchasePricePercentageOfVolumeWeightedAveragePriceForThreeConsecutiveDayTradingPeriod" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">97.5</ix:nonFraction>%. The maximum number of shares the Company could sell to New Circle on any single business day was the lesser of (i) the number of&#160;shares equal to <em style="font: inherit;">100%</em>&#160;of the average daily trading volume of the common stock of the Company during the <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> trading days immediately preceding the purchase notice, and (ii) <ix:nonFraction id="c145963809" contextRef="i_2024-07-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="lidr:EquityOfferingMaximumSharesPerDay" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">400,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of common stock.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In connection with the CSPA, the Company issued to New Circle&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145963810" contextRef="d_2024-07-25_2024-07-25_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">225,563</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of common stock&#160;in the Company as commitment shares for the facility. The Company determined that the right to sell additional shares represented&#160;a freestanding put option under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">815,</em> <i>Derivatives and Hedging</i>, and as such, the financial instrument was classified as a derivative asset with a fair value of <em style="font: inherit;">zero</em>&#160;at inception of the CSPA on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 25, 2024</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">This CSPA agreement was terminated in <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025. </em>In total, the Company issued <ix:nonFraction id="c145963813" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">8,980,713</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of its common stock, including commitment&#160;shares,&#160;for gross proceeds totaling $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963814" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_CounterpartyNameAxis-NewCirclePrincipalInvestmentsLLCMember_SubsidiarySaleOfStockAxis-SharePurchaseAgreementMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodValueNewIssues" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">27,754</ix:nonFraction>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b>Alliance Global Partners (</b>&#8220;<b>A.G.P.</b>&#8221;<b>)</b> <b>At Market Issuance Sales Agreement (the </b>&#8220;<b>ATM Agreement</b>&#8221;<b>)</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> September 12, 2024</em>, the Company entered into the ATM and a Registration Rights Agreement with A.G.P. Under the terms and subject to the conditions of the ATM Agreement,&#160;the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue and sell through A.G.P. the Company&#8217;s common stock having an aggregate value offering price of up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963816"    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;"><i><b>Market-Based Restricted Stock Uni</b>ts</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2026,&#160;</em>the Board of Directors approved grants totaling <ix:nonFraction id="c145963878" contextRef="i_2026-02-28_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-The2021EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,248,426</ix:nonFraction> market-based RSUs&#160;to certain executive officers of the Company that vest based on satisfaction of certain market conditions&#160;and upon continued service (&#8220;PSU Awards&#8221;). The PSU Awards will vest in increments of <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145963881"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145963897"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145963898">third</span></span></span> of the total grant when the closing price of the Company's common stock, as reported by NASDAQ, (i) meets or exceeds an average of <em style="font: inherit;">$3.00</em> per share for any <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> (<em style="font: inherit;">5</em>) consecutive trading days, (ii) meets or exceeds an average of <em style="font: inherit;">$4.00</em> per share for any <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> (<em style="font: inherit;">5</em>) consecutive trading days, and (iii) meets or exceeds an average of <em style="font: inherit;">$5.00</em> per share for any <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> (<em style="font: inherit;">5</em>) consecutive trading days, prior to <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2030. </em>To the extent common stock is available under the <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Equity Incentive Plan ("the Plan"), common stock will be used to settle vested PSU Awards on a prorated basis for all participants on the settlement date.&#160; Otherwise, vested PSU Awards will be settled in cash equal to the fair market value of common stock on the settlement date, defined as the <em style="font: inherit;">five</em>-day trailing average of the closing price of the stock as reported by NASDAQ.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company has&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145963918">one</span>&#160;reportable segment managed on a consolidated basis by the Chief Executive Officer&#160;who is the chief operating decision maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;). In identifying&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;reportable segment, the Company considered the basis of organization for the design and development of high-performance, active lidar systems and&#160;applications.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The accounting policies of the segment are the same as those described in the summary of significant accounting policies. The CODM assesses performance and decides how to allocate resources based on consolidated net loss as reported in the consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive loss.&#160; There are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> other expense categories regularly provided to the&#160;CODM&#160;that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> already included in the consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive loss. The measure of segment assets is reported on the balance sheet as cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Contract Liabilities</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company had <ix:nonFraction id="c145963936" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerLiability" scale="3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction>&#160;contract liabilities&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Remaining Performance Obligations</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations represents the transaction price allocated to the performance obligations that are unsatisfied, or partially unsatisfied. It includes unearned revenue and amounts that will be invoiced and recognized as revenue in future periods and does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include contracts where the customer is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> committed. The customer is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered committed where they are able to terminate for convenience without payment of a substantive penalty under the contract. Additionally, as a practical expedient, the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> disclosed the value of unsatisfied performance obligations for contracts with an original expected length of <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year or less.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 1pt;text-indent:36pt;">For the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, the Company recognized $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963969" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963970" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;provision for income taxes, respectively. The income tax rates vary from the federal and state statutory rates due to the valuation allowances on the Company&#8217;s net operating losses and foreign tax rate differences. The Company computes its quarterly income tax provision by using a forecasted annual effective tax rate and adjusts for any discrete items arising during the quarter.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Legal matters</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be subject to legal proceedings and claims that arise in the ordinary course of business.&#160;Litigation&#160;can be expensive and disruptive to normal business operations. Moreover, the results of complex legal proceedings are difficult to predict and the Company&#8217;s view of these matters <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>change in the future as the litigation and events related thereto unfold. The Company expenses legal fees as incurred.&#160;The Company records a provision for contingent losses when it is both probable that a liability has been incurred and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> the Company was notified by a former vendor that it intended to pursue a claim against the Company&#8217;s wholly owned subsidiary, AEye Technologies, Inc., arising out of an agreement entered into in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> May 2020</em><i>,</i>&#160;in which the former vendor alleges that AEye Technologies, Inc. failed to pay approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c145963977" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_LitigationCaseAxis-FailureOfPaymentMember_LitigationStatusAxis-PendingLitigationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyEstimateOfPossibleLoss" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3,300</ix:nonFraction>&#160;plus&#160;interest from the date the former vendor alleges such payments were due.&#160;In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 2026,&#160;</em>the former vendor initiated a binding arbitration proceeding against AEye Technologies, Inc. pursuant to the underlying purchase agreement. AEye Technologies, Inc. has disputed, and continues to dispute, the total amount owed based, in part, on the claim that the products supplied by the former vendor were largely defective and such former vendor was repeatedly made aware of the existence of such defects.&#160;While it is reasonably possible that a loss&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>be incurred, the Company is unable to estimate the possible loss or range of loss that could result from an unfavorable outcome in this legal proceeding.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Overview</b></p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">This overview provides a high-level discussion of our operating results and some of the trends that affect our business. We believe that an understanding of these trends is important to understanding our financial results for the three months ended March 31, 2026, as well as our future prospects. This summary is not intended to be exhaustive, nor is it intended to be a substitute for the detailed discussion and analysis provided elsewhere in this Quarterly Report, including our condensed consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes.</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Market Trends and Uncertainties</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We anticipate growing demand for our Apollo<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>&#160;platform across our two major markets,&#160;Automotive and Non-Automotive, and we believe this expected growth will enable us to capture market share across both the Automotive and Non-Automotive markets. We plan to pursue opportunities in advanced driver-assistance systems, or ADAS, autonomous driving, and commercial trucking, while also exploring opportunities in the Non-Automotive market, such as in the railway, airport safety and security, perimeter monitoring, aerospace and defense, transportation logistics, and intelligent transportation systems, or ITS, segments. This diversified approach provides us with multiple opportunities for sustained growth by enabling new applications and product features across a broad range of industries and market segments. However, as our customers continue their R&amp;D projects to commercialize solutions that rely on lidar technology, it is difficult to estimate the timing of ultimate end market demand&#160;and customer adoption.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In the Automotive market for example, our growth and financial performance will be heavily influenced by our ability to successfully integrate into OEM programs that require years of development, testing, and validation. Because of the size and complexity of these OEM programs, having Tier 1 partnerships should provide a substantial competitive advantage over our competitors given their large scale, mass-production capabilities, and existing OEM relationships held by our Tier 1 partners. If we fail to remain engaged with one or more Tier 1 automotive suppliers, it may have an adverse effect on our business. The Automotive market&#160;for lidar is projected to see significant growth in&#160;the mid-&#160;and long-term.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We anticipate that Non&#8209;Automotive applications will be a more significant driver of our near&#8209;term revenue given the generally shorter sales cycles and development timelines in these markets. We are beginning to&#160;see&#160;adoption across a diverse group of sectors. Our typical engagement model begins with proof&#8209;of&#8209;concept evaluations, which allow customers to validate performance in their operational environments; however, there is no guarantee that these evaluations will ultimately result in a commercial deployment, and timelines may extend significantly,&#160;due to many factors, including, competing customer priorities or broader program changes. In many Non&#8209;Automotive opportunities, we work through third&#8209;party systems integrators or solution providers who deliver complete solutions to the end customer, and in those situations our visibility into, and ability to influence, the final customer decision process may be limited.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Partnerships and Commercialization</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Our technology is designed to be a key enabler in certain Automotive and Non-Automotive&#160;market applications. Because our technology must be integrated into a broader solution by our customers, it is critical that we achieve design wins with these customers. The time to achieve a design win varies based on the market and application. We consider design wins to be critical to our future success, although the revenue that may be generated by each design win and the time necessary to achieve such a design win can vary significantly, making it difficult to predict our financial performance. We have&#160;unified&#160;our supply chain for the Automotive and Non-Automotive markets and plan to leverage our Tier 1 automotive suppliers to produce products for us to sell into&#160;our Non-Automotive markets, whereas in the Automotive markets, we anticipate licensing our technology to our Tier 1 suppliers in exchange for a royalty.&#160;The unified supply chain should allow us to leverage the scale, efficiencies, and volume associated with supplying the Automotive market to benefit our Non-Automotive market customers. In 2023, as part of our effort to reduce fixed operating costs, simplify our supply chain, and focus resources on our next&#8209;generation architecture, we wound down support for our legacy Non&#8209;Automotive product. Since launching Apollo<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>&#160;in 2024, we have seen renewed interest from Non&#8209;Automotive customers across a broad range of sectors and are now actively engaged on multiple opportunities.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In early 2024, we engaged LITEON as our Tier 1 automotive supplier and are actively working with LITEON to bring our product to market. We&#160;announced&#160;an expansion of this relationship and the creation of a dedicated production line for Apollo<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>, with capacity to produce up to 60,000 units annually. We are starting to see an inflection point in customer demand, and this expansion ensures we can meet that growth if&#160;it develops.&#160;This partnership enables&#160;us to leverage LITEON&#8217;s manufacturing expertise to produce high-quality products that meet stringent performance standards, which is a critical step towards scaling production and delivering our advanced lidar solutions to the market.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In May 2024, we announced a strategic partnership with&#160;Accelight Technologies, Inc. ("ATI") and LighTekton Co., Ltd to manufacture and distribute our products in China. This collaboration provides us with access to a potential $2.5 billion market opportunity. By leveraging ATI's and LighTekton's extensive networks and manufacturing capabilities, we aim to accelerate our market penetration and deliver our advanced lidar solutions to a broader audience.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">In July 2025, we announced the validation&#160;of our lidar technology on the NVIDIA&#160;DRIVE AGX Orin<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup> platform. We have since expanded our collaboration and demonstrated our lidar with NVIDIA's next-generation DRIVE AGX Thor<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup> platform, enabling our sensors to interface directly with NVIDIA&#8217;s autonomous driving compute architecture and development toolchain. These integrations are intended to support alignment with NVIDIA&#8217;s Hyperion reference architecture and may provide opportunities to engage with global automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers that adopt NVIDIA&#8209;based ADAS and automated driving systems. We continue to demonstrate advances in the high&#8209;speed and long&#8209;range performance of our lidar systems, which we believe further strengthen the technical basis for these integrations. Because these engagements are relatively recent, there can be no guarantee that they will result in commercial adoption.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In July 2025, we launched OPTIS&#8482;, a complete physical AI solution designed to modernize legacy infrastructure and deliver actionable intelligence across diverse industries. OPTIS&#8482; integrates our software-defined Apollo<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>&#160;lidar technology with advanced computing to bridge the gap between perception and real-time action. Beyond addressing critical needs in transportation, safety, and security, OPTIS&#8482; opens our platform to third-party partners and developers, creating an ecosystem for innovation and growth beyond automotive applications. Since launch, we&#8217;ve transitioned OPTIS&#8482; from concept to a structured offering, with initial deployments already completed. Our flagship OPTIS&#8482; deployment&#160;in&#160;California&#160;is live at an active intersection and provides the potential for a complete traffic management solution that integrates our lidar, perception, and actuation in conjunction with our partners Flasheye and Blue-Band, with several additional deployments planned. Recent additions to our partner network include Black Sesame Technologies and Vueron.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In January 2026, we introduced&#160;STRATOS&#8482;, the next product in our lidar family. STRATOS&#8482; is based on the same underlying software&#8209;defined Apollo<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>&#160;architecture but delivers an extended detection range of up to&#160;approximately 1.5 kilometers and roughly twice the angular resolution. STRATOS&#8482; is designed for applications requiring enhanced long&#8209;distance performance, including sensing requirements in&#160;certain automotive, infrastructure, aviation, industrial, and defense use cases.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In March 2026, we joined the NVIDIA Halos AI Systems Inspection Lab, the world&#8217;s first ANAB-accredited AI systems inspection lab, which we believe further reinforces our positioning within the NVIDIA ecosystem and may support our engagement with global automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers. Also, during the first quarter of 2026, we entered into a commercial relationship with SynTech, a global defense systems company with established ties to leading defense primes, under which SynTech began promoting Apollo&#8482; to its customers and we have commenced initial shipments. We believe this relationship could expand our addressable market into international defense and aviation; however, there can be no assurance that this relationship, or the integrations described above, will result in commercial sales for us.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In aerospace and defense, our customer engagements continued to ramp during the first quarter of 2026, with multiple repeat orders from existing customers and active development across multiple programs with certain customers. We are evaluating expanded use cases for our products with these customers, and we expect to receive additional requests for quotation in the near term. While we are encouraged by the trajectory of these engagements, there can be no assurance that they will translate into commercial sales for us.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We believe our revenue and profitability will also be dependent upon our success in licensing our technology to Tier 1 automotive suppliers, such as our current Tier 1 partner, LITEON, and these partners securing program awards from OEMs&#160;and scaling to high volume production of our lidar sensors. Delays in&#160;autonomy programs by OEMs that we are currently or plan to be&#160;working with through our Tier 1 partners could result in us being unable to achieve our revenue and profitability targets in the time frame we anticipate, or at all.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt;"><b><i>Geographic Opportunities</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">While our commercial activities remain primarily focused in North America, we are also actively engaging with customers in EMEA and APAC. Our APAC strategy has begun to evolve through business development activities in Korea, where we have established on-the-ground support and have engaged with multiple customers across the ITS, rail, and mobility sectors. In China, we have multiple customer evaluations in progress, supported by our existing partnerships with ATI and LighTekton. Additional proof-of-concept activity is underway in other geographies, including Australia and Thailand. There can be no assurance that any of these international engagements will result in commercial sales for us.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Gross Margin</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Our gross margins will depend on numerous factors, including, among others, the selling price of our products, pricing of our development contracts with customers, royalty rates on licenses we grant to our customers, unit volumes, product mix, component costs, personnel costs, contract manufacturing costs, overhead costs, and product features. Our gross margins have and may continue to be&#160;negatively impacted by inventory write-downs. In the future, we expect to generate attractive gross margins from licensing our lidar technology and software to our Tier 1 partners in the Automotive market. We also anticipate being able to leverage on our foundation in the Automotive market to be more cost competitive in other markets.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">To date, we have primarily generated revenue through sales of our products to Non&#8209;Automotive customers and through development contracts with OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers. Non&#8209;Automotive applications typically command higher average selling prices and may carry higher gross margins than Automotive programs due to lower volume sensitivity, more specialized operating requirements, and greater willingness by customers to pay for performance differentiation. These engagements often involve customization of our product&#8217;s capabilities to address application&#8209;specific needs, including software&#8209;based configuration of scan patterns, region&#8209;of&#8209;interest tuning, advanced perception features, and other enhancements. In many cases, customers require more complex configurations or software&#8209;enabled feature additions, which allows us greater latitude to price these solutions at a premium. As a result, customized Non&#8209;Automotive deployments generally reflect higher contractual pricing and may contribute more favorably to gross margin relative to standard Automotive configurations.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Investment and Innovation</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Our proprietary adaptive intelligent lidar technology delivers industry-leading performance, addressing the toughest challenges in achieving partial or full autonomy. Unlike traditional sensing systems that passively collect data, our active Intelligent Sensing Platform employs principles from automated targeting systems and biomimicry to actively scan the environment, intelligently focusing on critical elements to enable safer, smarter, and faster decisions in complex scenarios.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Our next&#8209;generation lidar portfolio is built on our Intelligent Sensing Platform, a modular and software&#8209;defined architecture that allows us to create differentiated product offerings with limited incremental hardware changes. By maintaining a common core design and enabling performance enhancements through software&#8212;such as configurable scan patterns, range distribution, and perception features&#8212;we are able to address diverse application requirements while minimizing the operational complexity typically associated with managing a large product portfolio. This platform&#8209;based approach also allows us to introduce new products efficiently. For example, STRATOS&#8482;, launched in January 2026, is derived from the Apollo's<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>&#160;architecture but offers extended range and higher angular resolution to support long&#8209;distance and higher&#8209;performance applications.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In June 2024, we introduced Apollo<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>, our next generation lidar sensor. Apollo<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>&#160;offers best-in-class range and resolution in a compact, power-efficient, and cost-effective form factor, making it ideal for both automotive and non-automotive applications. Apollo<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>&#160;can be integrated behind the windshield, on the roof, or in the grille, allowing OEMs to implement essential safety features with minimal impact on vehicle design. This innovative sensor leverages our Intelligent Sensing Platform, providing a highly programmable and customizable lidar solution that can be continually enhanced via software updates. With a horizontal field of view up to 120&#176; and long-range detection capabilities of up to one kilometer, Apollo<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>&#160;is poised to be a key&#160;player in advancing vehicle safety and autonomy, as well as smart infrastructure and logistics applications.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Building on this foundation, we launched OPTIS&#8482; in July 2025, a complete physical AI solution that extends our capabilities beyond automotive. OPTIS&#8482; combines Apollo&#8217;s<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>&#160;software-defined lidar with advanced computing to deliver actionable intelligence for modernizing legacy infrastructure. This platform not only addresses critical needs in transportation, safety, and security but also opens our ecosystem to third-party partners and developers, fostering innovation across industries. Since launch, OPTIS&#8482; has moved from concept to structured offering, with initial deployments completed and new partners such as Black Sesame Technologies, BlueBand, Flasheye, and Vueron joining our network.&#160;In addition, in January 2026, we announced STRATOS&#8482;, the next product in this family. STRATOS&#8482; is based on the same underlying architecture as Apollo&#8482; but offers extended detection range of up to approximately 1.5 kilometers and roughly twice the angular resolution. STRATOS&#8482; is intended for applications that require enhanced long&#8209;distance performance or operate at higher speeds, including certain automotive, infrastructure, defense, and industrial sensing environments. Like Apollo&#8482;, STRATOS&#8482; leverages our software&#8209;defined sensing approach, enabling performance updates without a hardware redesign.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">We believe our financial performance is significantly dependent on our ability to maintain a technology leadership position. This is further dependent on the investments we make in research and development and our ability to commercialize our products. We believe price is becoming a critical differentiator in the marketplace and OEMs are favoring companies that have the infrastructure to build lower cost products at higher volumes. It is essential that we continually identify and respond to rapidly evolving customer requirements, develop and introduce innovative new products, enhance and service existing products, lower bill of materials, or BOM costs, industrialize&#160;the manufacturing process, and generate strong market demand for our products. If we fail to do this, our market position and revenue may be adversely affected, and our investments in that area will not be recovered.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Basis of Presentation </b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">We currently conduct our business through one operating segment.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Components of Results of Operations</b><b><i> </i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Revenues </i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Our product&#160;revenue primarily relates&#160;to unit sales of our lidar units, software, and support. Revenue from these&#160;sales is typically recognized at a point in time when the control of the goods is transferred to the customer, generally upon delivery of or shipment to the customer, or when services have been provided.&#160;Revenue from development and/or collaboration contracts are earned from R&amp;D activities and collaboration with OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers. These contracts primarily focus on customization of our product's capabilities to our customers&#8217; applications, typically involving software implementation to assist with sensor connection and control, customization of scan patterns, and enhancement of perception capabilities to meet specific customer needs. Revenue from development contracts is recognized when we satisfy performance obligations in the contract, which can result in recognition at either a point in time or over time. This assessment is made at the outset of the arrangement for each performance obligation.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We are seeing strong&#160;interest in Apollo<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>&#160;from non-automotive customers across multiple industries and are actively advancing these opportunities.&#160;Proof-of-concept deployments are validating our technology in real-world scenarios, creating a solid foundation for future growth. While customer evaluation and testing cycles are typically extended, these engagements position us well for gradual revenue contributions and set the stage for meaningful expansion through higher volume programs. We view this as the first step in a disciplined growth roadmap designed to unlock adoption and scale with confidence.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Several partners are also exploring new platforms based on our Apollo<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>&#160;architecture and have initiated discussions on development work, which we expect will increase over time.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Cost of Revenue</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">Cost of revenue includes costs directly associated with the production of lidar units, cost of software and support, and certain costs associated with development contracts. Such costs for the&#160;products include direct materials, direct labor, indirect labor, inventory write downs, losses on purchase commitments, warranty expense, and allocation of overhead. As we increase the volume of Apollo<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">TM</sup>&#160;units that are manufactured, we expect the bill of material costs to decrease over time. Costs associated with development contracts include the direct costs and allocation of overhead costs involved in the execution of the contracts.&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Change in Fair Value of Convertible Note and Warrant Liabilities</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The changes&#160;in fair value of the convertible note and warrant liabilities are the result of the change in fair value at each reporting date. The convertible note&#160;and warrant liabilities were recorded at fair value for each reporting period, and the changes in fair value were reported within other income (expense), net during the period. We also elected to record interest expense on the&#160;convertible note as changes in fair value.&#160;We have fully repaid the 2025 convertible note and will not have a change in fair value of the convertible note in future periods.&#160;In addition, we expect the change in fair value of&#160;warrant liabilities&#160;to decrease as&#160;the warrant&#160;associated with the 2022 convertible note was cancelled and the warrant&#160;associated with the 2025 convertible note was exercised in full.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Interest Income, Interest Expense and Other </i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Interest income and other consists primarily of interest and investment income earned on our cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. These amounts will vary based on our cash,&#160;cash equivalents, and marketable securities balances and market rates. Interest income and other also includes gains on sale of property and equipment. Interest expense and other consists primarily of financing costs, amortization of premiums and accretion of discounts on marketable securities, net, and foreign exchange gains and losses.&#160;</p>
